---
title: "Core concepts before code"
description: "The sample, layer, integration, annotation, and inference concepts that prevent invalid single-cell conclusions."
---

# Core concepts before code

## Cells are observations; samples are experimental units

A matrix may contain 100,000 cells but only six patients. For a treatment or disease contrast, the effective replication is usually six biological samples—not 100,000 independent cells. Keep `sample_id`, `patient_id`, and `condition` throughout the object.

## QC is a distributional decision

Compute QC metrics first, view them per sample, then choose and record thresholds. Mitochondrial percentage, detected genes, UMI count, doublet score, ambient RNA, and outlier rules answer different failure modes. A universal `percent.mt < 20` line is not a quality-control strategy.

## Seurat v5 layers must be deliberate

Merged objects can retain split layers. Join them before functions that expect one counts/data layer:

```r
srt <- JoinLayers(srt)
Layers(srt[[DefaultAssay(srt)]])
```

## Integration is a correction with a risk

Integration aims to reduce unwanted source variation while preserving biology. Validate both sides:

- **source mixing** should improve when source is unwanted;
- **cell-type or condition structure** should remain coherent;
- markers should remain biologically interpretable;
- the target biological contrast must not be supplied as the batch variable.

## Annotation is evidence synthesis

No single automated label is ground truth. Combine canonical markers, cluster markers, reference mapping, model confidence, tissue context, and doublet/low-quality signals. Keep uncertain and mixed labels instead of forcing every cell into a confident class.

## Differential expression follows the design

- Cluster markers explain a cluster and may use cell-level tests.
- Exploratory state markers compare cells and must be labelled exploratory.
- Study-level condition inference should aggregate counts to `sample × cell type` and fit a sample-level model.
- A dataset-source contrast is not a disease contrast.

## Spatial spots are mixtures

Visium spots can contain several cells. Spatial domains, Moran features, neighbourhood associations, and deconvolution have different interpretations. Do not call a spot-level label a cell type without a cell-resolved method and appropriate evidence.
